text:
Maya: FYI customer hitting invalid JSON parse in structured JSON mode for orders API. They say client crashes when parsing items array.
Alex: can you paste the raw response they got + request id? also which model and json_mode flags?
Maya: pasted below. model: rwd-3-small. json_mode: structured, strict_schema=true. request_id: r-7f3a2c.
Maya: ```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "orders": [
    {"id": "ord_101", "total": 42.5},
    {"total": 13.0, "legacy_meta": {"source": "import"}},
    {"id": "ord_103", "total": 0.0, "notes": null}
  ]
}
```
Maya: client expects every item to have an id (required in their schema). second item missing id -> parser fails. They say this behavior started after last runtime deploy.
Chris: are we supposed to be dropping/omitting required fields when generating? That sounds like schema drift in the model output.
support-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-3147 (linked to request r-7f3a2c)
Danielle: Also customer reports auth token 401s intermittently around same time and a billing spike entry at 2024-11-05T14:02Z for that workspace. Could be retry storms.
Alex: repro attempt: I ran the same prompt with strict_schema=true and got a similar item missing id about 15% of the time. Repro steps:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3-small","mode":"structured","schema":"orders_schema_v2","prompt":"export orders list","strict_schema":true,"stream":false}'
```
Alex: response sample attached (same missing id).
eng-qa: I can reproduce locally on canary runtime. Looks like when the model returns an extra key inside the second item (legacy_meta) we drop id sometimes. Hypothesis: token-level prefix caching + aggressive streaming boundary trimmed the id token when the model emitted legacy_meta first.
Chris: does this align with the runtime change on 2024-11-04? Ben, Liu any idea? @Ben @Liu
Ben: pinged. Quick note: our recent streaming patch changed how we flush partial top-level arrays to avoid latency regressions. Might have introduced boundary trimming for nested arrays.
Liu: looking into the model conditioning too — the model may sometimes reorder fields. strict_schema currently enforces presence but our postprocessor aborts instead of attempting a safe fix.
Danielle: Customer is asking for immediate mitigation. They want either: 1) server-side auto-fill missing required ids with temp ids, OR 2) fallback to non-strict mode for that workspace. Also they want billing credit for the spike while we troubleshoot.
Alex: short-term: we can set strict_schema=false for that workspace and add a per-workspace rollout. I can push a config change. Need SRE to confirm rollout.
Maya: please also provide the customer with repro steps and a safe parsing recommendation (client-side tolerant parse).
eng-qa: proposed fix items: revert the streaming flush change (hotfix) OR make postprocessor tolerant by backfilling missing required fields with temp_id and emitting a warning trace. Both require eng-runtime review.
Ben: I'll prepare a hotfix PR to prevent trimming nested tokens. If we can ship within 2 hours we should avoid more client crashes.
Liu: I'll add a model-side alignment test to reduce field reordering for structured mode.
Alex: @support-bot mark customer workspace for billing review and tag finance. Also add a note to the incident that strict_schema=false rollout was applied at 2024-11-05T15:10Z as mitigation.
support-bot: Incident INC-2024-3147 updated: mitigation applied, finance tagged.
Maya: I'll send the customer an update: apology, mitigation steps, repro steps to reduce crashes (client-tolerant parse + retry with validate).
Chris: keep this thread updated with PR and deploy links.
Maya: thanks all.
